next_guide.basis: Q3's guide implied 11.4-15.2% YoY. The same band on Q4 2025's $581.9m gives $646-670m, midpoint about $658m, against the unconfirmed $645.5m street figure. Ad-network peers guided Q4 strongly (AppLovin +43-44%, Unity strategic +65-67%), and BIGO Ads went live as an AdMob bidding partner on 2026-10-13. Against that, social entertainment was guided to only moderate single-digit growth.

findings.finding: JOYY has beaten the top of its own revenue guide three quarters running: Q4 2025 $581.9m against $563-578m, Q1 2026 $555.7m against $538-548m, Q2 2026 $590.8m against $562-581m (0.7-1.7% above the top). The same habit on the $602-622m Q3 guide points to about $628-632m, roughly 3% above the $608-612m consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat consensus revenue by about 3.6% and raised the operating-income target; stock -0.25%. Q1 2026 beat the top of the guide; +17.77%, mostly on the $1.5bn return plan. Q4 2025 beat by 2.7%; +2.26%. Revenue beats alone have been bought modestly or not at all.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits at $608-612m, inside the lower half of the guide, although the company has printed above the top three times. If the habit were priced, consensus would sit at or above $622m. It is priced in part: the whisper EPS of $1.42 sits above consensus, and a beat is the market's base case.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 actuals and guides: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/680470/joyy-reports-4q-and-fy2025-financial-results-q4-revenue-returns-to-yoy-growth-bigo-ads-up-61-5-yoy and https://www.rttnews.com/3655233/joyy-q1-income-from-cont-opns-up-issues-q2-view-plans-upto-600-mln-share-buyback-stock-up.aspx?type=corp (company releases, not an independent series)

findings.finding: Mobile in-app ad networks printed very strong Q3 2026 results after JOYY's August call. AppLovin revenue was $2.185bn, +55% YoY, about $100m above the top of its own August guide, with a Q4 guide of +43-44%. Unity's Grow segment rose 44% and its Vector ad network 126%. That points to strong BIGO Ads revenue (23% of JOYY revenue, guided only to 'strong double-digit' growth for Q3).
findings.link: Same market: BIGO Ads/BIGO Audience Network is a mobile in-app ad network (SDK in 55,000+ apps including game publishers Voodoo and TapNation), competing for the same in-app ad budgets as AppLovin and Unity Ads. It is a competitor, not a customer or supplier. BIGO Ads was $133.7m of $590.8m Q2 revenue (22.6%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BIGO Ads growth has been the stock's re-rating driver. Q3 2025 'BIGO Ads +33%' coincided with +6.26% (baseline 2025-11-20). Q2 2026 BIGO Ads +53% coincided with -0.25%.
findings.why_not_priced: These are proxies: the peers' Q3 strength is visible, but JOYY's Q3 consensus moved only from $601.7m to $608.2m and the stock fell 7% in 20 days. If the read-across were priced, consensus would sit near or above the top of the guide. BIGO's third-party Audience Network growth slowed (83% to 79% to 74%), which an investor could read as share loss against AppLovin.
findings.independence: Unity Q3 2026, a separate source: https://mobilegamer.biz/unity-posts-first-profit-since-its-ipo-as-vector-grows-126/ . Both are peers and neither is a JOYY number.

findings.finding: Yalla Group, the MENA voice-chat and live-room peer, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-16. Revenue was $90.4m, +0.9%, but chatting revenue fell 9.4% to $50.3m and spend per payer fell 5%. That is a soft read on Middle East live/voice monetisation, where JOYY credited new voice products for Q2's sequential growth.
findings.link: Same product and region: Bigo's Middle East voice-room products against Yalla's chat rooms. The Middle East was about 13% of JOYY revenue in H1 2025 (company presentation, 2025-10-20, https://www-web.itiger.com/news/2576381882). No shared customers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Social entertainment and live streaming have been the slow line (Q2 +7.4%). The stock has not reacted visibly to it since BIGO Ads became the story. No specific reaction to a live-streaming miss is on record.
findings.why_not_priced: Yalla printed two days before JOYY, so consensus cannot have moved on it. But JOYY already guided social entertainment to only 'moderate single-digit' growth, so the bar for this line is low. Net of the rest of the company, about 87% of revenue is outside the Middle East, and BIGO Ads and Shopline grow 25-50%.
findings.independence: none (one secondary summary of Yalla's release, not cross-checked against the PR Newswire text)

findings.finding: On 2026-10-13, after the last call, BIGO Ads became generally available as a Google AdMob mediation bidding partner across five ad formats, with an AI-app publisher reporting 2x ARPU from BIGO Ads in testing. It is a new demand-and-supply channel that management can cite in the Q4 BIGO Ads outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of a reaction to a partnership release. The stock's response to BIGO Ads guidance is positive on the record (see the peer finding).
findings.why_not_priced: A product release with no revenue figure, so no model can carry it yet. The call is the first place management can put a number on it. If priced, Q4 BIGO Ads estimates would have risen in October; the visible revisions only touch Q3 revenue (+$6.5m).

findings.finding: Q4 2026 guide: Q3's guide implied 11.4-15.2% YoY. The same band on Q4 2025's $581.9m gives $646-670m (midpoint about $658m), against the only street figure found, $645.5m (unconfirmed, unlabeled). Management also raised the full-year operating-income target in August, and its pattern since Q1 has been guides at or above the street, which points to a Q4 guide at or above consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2026 guide ($602-622m) set above the $591.8-601.7m consensus, with the operating-income target raised: -0.25%. Q1 2026 guide ($538-548m) set below the $551m consensus: +2.26% on the day (with the dividend/return news). The guide has not reliably moved the stock either way.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's Q4 number is barely visible: one unlabeled source, with a stale full-year $2.31bn below what Q1-Q3 already track to. If the street had rolled the 11-15% growth band forward, Q4 consensus would sit near $655m. Capped small because the bar is unsourced.
findings.independence: Q3 guide band: https://www.webull.com/news/15505960542266368 (call transcript). Peer Q4 guides (AppLovin +43-44%) point the same way for the ad line.

findings.finding: Management said on the August call to expect Q3 unrealized FX losses similar to H1 (Q2 was $14m) if the dollar kept weakening. The New York Fed's Q3 2026 FX report says the broad dollar ended the quarter little changed, so the Q3 FX loss may be smaller than modelled, lifting GAAP and possibly non-GAAP net income.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Net income fell YoY in Q2 (non-GAAP EPS $1.24 vs $1.44) while operating income rose 28%; the stock reacted -0.25%. Below-the-line items have not visibly moved it.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission JOYY has not confirmed. Its FX exposure is by currency pair and the broad dollar is a proxy. EPS consensus is dispersed ($1.30-1.42), which suggests some analysts carry an FX loss and some do not.
findings.independence: Trading Economics (snippet): DXY up 1.5% in September, little changed over Q3. Same direction, weak.

findings.finding: Expectations: the stock gave back 7% in 20 days to $78.60, 7.5% under its $85.15 high and about 9-14% under the $85-89 mean target. Over the same period the Q3 revenue consensus rose from $601.7m to $608.2m and the whisper EPS sits above consensus, so the price bar fell while the estimate bar rose.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 print came off a lower base and returned +17.77%. The Q2 print came after a run to a then-high (JPM upgrade 2026-08-12) and returned -0.25%.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown has no identified company-specific cause (none found). KWEB was down about 6% over the month to Oct 26, so part of it is the sector. A pullback into a print lowers the bar the price holds. It is not evidence by itself, so sized small.
findings.independence: Baseline tape (run_up_20d -7.05%) and https://www.etfcentral.com/fund/KWEB for the sector.

findings.finding: Capital return: as of 2026-08-21, $471.6m of the 2026 buyback authorization remained, against $3.06bn of net cash, inside a $1.5bn 2026-28 return plan. $359m was returned year to date ($216m buybacks), and management said shareholders can expect 'greater returns in the long run' as operating profit grows. A Q3 dividend (Q2 was $1.55 per ADS) and possibly an upsized return plan can come with the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 release introduced the $1.5bn return plan and $600m buyback; stock +17.77%, the largest reaction on record.
findings.why_not_priced: The existing plan is priced. Any upsizing is not known. Net cash of $3.06bn is about 80% of the market cap (48.97m ADS-equivalents x $78.60 is about $3.85bn), which leaves room for a step-up, but no source says one is coming.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-04 Pakistan's PTA formally registered BIGO LIVE and Likee, reopening a market where Bigo had been blocked since 2020. Small, inside Q4.
findings.why_not_priced: Local-press story with no revenue figure. Pakistan is likely immaterial to a $2.4bn revenue base unless management mentions it.

findings.finding: The EPS line carries below-OI risk. In Q2, non-GAAP operating income rose 28% to $49.1m while non-GAAP net income fell 17.5% to $63.5m (EPS $1.24 vs $1.44), on FX losses and lower interest income as net cash fell from $3.26bn to $3.06bn with buybacks. Q3 EPS consensus is dispersed ($1.30-1.42), and the gross margin (34.1% vs 36.5%) is diluting with mix. Q4 2025 non-GAAP EPS reportedly missed ($1.34 vs $1.40).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 EPS miss with a revenue beat: +2.26% per baseline (a secondary site says -2.87%; the two disagree). Q2 2026 EPS beat with net income down YoY: -0.25%.
findings.why_not_priced: Zacks flags margin dilution as the key debate, so this is partly priced. The EPS bar is unsourced (three figures disagree), so it is capped small. It shares its source with the FX finding but concerns interest income and mix, not FX.

baseline_tension: The evidence leans mildly positive, which agrees with the call-bid skew (unusable spread) and cuts against the -7% 20-day run-up. Agreement with the skew means part of the lean is priced, which holds p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the beat-the-top-of-guide finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3, because the last beat and raise was sold (-0.25%).
Lesson 6 (unsourced bar): Q4 next-guide finding cut from +0.8 to +0.5, because the street Q4 figure has one unlabeled source.
Lesson 5 (proxies smaller): AppLovin/Unity read-across cut from +0.5 to +0.4.
Lesson 9 (size a segment net of the rest): Yalla/Middle East finding cut from -0.4 to -0.3, since the Middle East is about 13% of revenue and social entertainment was already guided low.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the FX finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1.

Lesson 1 again, on the scaled number: p_up from 57 to 56, abs_move unchanged at 5.5; expected_move from 0.77 to 0.66. Left standing: capital, expectations, positioning, regulatory and EPS-risk findings.
